title: A Scientific Claim Stability Framework for Evaluating MRI Morphometry Pipelines
claim: Conventional evaluation stops at measurement agreement; our claim-centric framework turns outputs into auditable claims tested under multiple perturbation axes.
layout: 5 lettered panels, left-to-right rows plus right column, zoom-in callouts
description: A dense multi-panel figure with five lettered sections. Panel A (top left, grey) shows conventional evaluation: an MRI image goes into a pipeline icon, then ROI tables, then grey arrows to scatter plot, agreement score and prediction metrics. Panel B repeats the flow in blue/purple, but ends in scientific claims, with a zoomed table listing claim types (contrast, association, ranking, latent) with support, stability and drift bars and colored tags. Panel C is a row of green and purple module icons (loading through review analysis) with a shaded 'Scientific layers' block and a feedback loop. Panel D, at top right, is a radial burst of five perturbation axes (dataset, pipeline, target, feature family, atlas) around a central 'SCS evaluation' node. Panel E shows a claim object and a detailed claim card with status badges. The eye goes first to the grey versus colored contrast between A and B.
caption: Overview of the Scientific Claim Stability framework. Conventional evaluation compares ROI measurements or prediction scores, whereas SCS converts ROI tables into claim cards and evaluates whether the resulting scientific conclusions remain supported under dataset, pipeline, atlas, feature-family, and target perturbations. Details in Appendix [ref].
abstract: MRI morphometry pipelines are often evaluated by measurement agreement or downstream accuracy, yet their scientific value depends on the conclusions they support. Two pipelines can produce similar feature-level results yet support different conclusions about aging, cognitive decline, or neurodegeneration. We introduce Scientific Claim Stability (SCS), a claim-centric evaluation framework that converts region-of-interest (ROI) morphometry tables into auditable claim cards and evaluates their support under changes in dataset, processing pipeline, atlas, feature family, and target. Across 10,370 MRI scans from three datasets and five cohorts, SCS generates 2,783 claim cards and evaluates 89 claim-family pairs. The evaluation distinguishes stable, transferable, and fragile claims. FreeSurfer 8-FastSurfer comparisons show high evidence concordance and low anatomical-support overlap under the primary covariate specification. Acquisition-adjusted analyses show that the magnitude of support disagreement depends on the model specification. Structured review by specialists in geriatrics, neuroscience, and radiology, alongside auxiliary ChatGPT and Gemini reviewers, assesses claim plausibility, clarity, faithfulness, usefulness, and caution. SCS provides a reproducible way to audit the evidential stability of morphometry claims without assuming a universal gold standard.
